sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant-petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter referred to as the 'APP') for the State, as well as learned counsel for the informant.

2. The sole appellant, who has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 302, 120B, 201, 498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for brevity 'IPC') and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs. 50,000/- under Sections 302/34 of the IPC; sentenced to undergo rigorous Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.691 of 2017(6) dt.16-08-2023 imprisonment for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs. 40,000/-
under Section 120B of the IPC

; sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and to pay a fine of Rs. 5,000/- under Sections 201/34 of the IPC; sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment Rizwan Ansari vs The State Of Bihar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164481985/
1 for 2 years and to pay a fine of Rs. 3,000/- under Sections 498A/34 of the IPC; sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 1 year and to pay a fine of Rs. 1,000/- under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and in case of default in payment of fine to further undergo an additional period of simple imprisonment for 6 months, has renewed his prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail during pendency of the appeal.

entities.text: Rizwan Ansari vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Earlier prayer for bail made on behalf of the instant appellant-petitioner was rejected on 17.07.2017.
The appellant- petitioner has remained in jail now for over 9 years.
4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant- petitioner that at the trial, there is no material to sustain the manner, the time, or the place at which the killing has occurred.
Based on an earlier complaint petition lodged by the victim four months prior to the incident, which culminated in a compromise, motive has been assigned.

P.W.2, cousin of the deceased, is the person who for the first time stated that he had received telephonic intimation regarding killing of the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.691 of 2017(6) dt.16-08-2023 informant's daughter, which he passed on to the informant.
At the trial, however, he has not stated the name of the person who had intimated him about the killing.
Otherwise, there is no material whatsoever to sustain the finding of killing of the informant's daughter.

It is further submitted that the death as per the prosecution has occurred more than nine years after the marriage and, therefore, the motive assigned regarding dowry is also unsustainable.
5.
Learned APP for the State as well as the learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail.
Written objection has been filed by the learned APP for the State.
It is submitted that the appellant-petitioner has not discharged burden under Section 106 of the Evidence Act.

6. This court finds that the appellant-petitioner's prayer was earlier considered on merits and rejected on 17.07.2017 with a direction for preparation of paper books so as to facilitate consideration of the appeal on merits.
Till date, the same has not been taken up, nor is there any likelihood of the same being taken up for hearing in the near future.

7. Considering the rival submission, the above noted facts and circumstances and the long period of custody, this Court, in light of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Saudan Singh v.
State of Uttar Pradesh reported in 2022 Patna High Court CR.

Saudan Singh v.
State of Uttar Pradesh reported in 2022 Patna High Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
APP (DB) No.691 of 2017(6)
dt.16-08-2023 SCC OnLine SC 697 as well as Kashmira Singh v. the State of Punjab reported in (1977) 4 SCC 291, is inclined to allow the prayer of appellant, since the appellant-petitioner has now remained in custody for nine years and one month.

entities.text: Kashmira Singh v. the State of Punjab reported in (1977) 4 SCC 291
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. The appellant-petitioner's prayer for bail and suspension of sentence during the pendency of this appeal is allowed.

9. Let the appellant-petitioner, above named, be released on bail during the pendency of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 5 th Additional Sessions Judge, Siwan in Sessions Trial No. 23 of 2015,
arising out of Basantpur P.S. Case No. 86 of 2012.
